summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — TSCO.L +7%, IMB.L +6%, AUTO.L +5%, BP.L +4%, G24.DE +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (FME.DE -12%, FRE.DE -6%, SDLF.L -5%, VOW3.DE -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: FME.DE (-11.89%) — No confirmed driver found for 2026-10-09. An -11.9% single-day drop in dialysis provider Fresenius Medical Care looks like a guidance cut or pre-announcement, but searches returned nothing dated today. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: FME.DE is a mid/large-cap German healthcare name on Xetra, and no strategy covers it. A sudden unscheduled gap-down also gives a long-only momentum or mean-reversion bot no entry signal.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed catalyst: searches found no Oct 9 news. Tesco's H1 results were reportedly due around Oct 8, so this may be a delayed reaction to them or a sector move, but I couldn't verify either.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: TSCO.L is a UK large-cap FTSE 100 consumer-staples stock, and no strategy includes it. A +7.4% day in a defensive grocer is also unusual and likely looked like a one-off event to the bot.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 staples such as TSCO.L to the momentum/news-reactive universe, and gate entries on a gap ≥ +3% on volume ≥ 1.5× the 20-day average. That would catch names making large moves after results.

top_movers.catalyst: Pre-close trading update: Imperial Brands on track for FY26 targets on all key metrics, plus a new £1.5bn FY27 buyback. Tobacco and defensives rallied while London fell on Brent above $105.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: IMB.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap defensive tobacco name, apparently not in any strategy's list. The move was a scheduled-update catalyst, so a post-announcement gap-up filter would also have been late.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 consumer-staples/tobacco (IMB.L, BATS.L) to the news-reactive universe, and let it enter on a trading update or buyback headline with a gap ≥ +3% on ≥1.5× average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day catalyst found. Likely a rebound in a heavily sold-off FTSE 100 stock (down about 38% over 1 year), possibly helped by buybacks or activist (Palliser) stake reports; none are dated today.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: AUTO.L is a FTSE 100 online-marketplace large cap that no strategy lists. A +4.9% rebound in a downtrending name with no clear news would also fail momentum and news-reactive filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 constituents to the momentum-trader universe, gated by a minimum 20-day-high or relative-strength rule. That would let oversold rebounds in large caps through only when a trend filter confirms them.

top_movers.catalyst: No BP-specific news found for 2026-10-09; likely an oil-price-driven sector move, since BP has been trading on Brent swings tied to Iran/Middle East headlines.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BP.L is a UK large-cap integrated oil major, and no strategy's universe includes UK/EU energy names. A +4.4% sector-beta move on oil would not have triggered a single-name news filter anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a UK energy basket (BP.L, SHEL.L) to the momentum universe and gate entry on Brent move ≥ +2% with BP.L volume ≥ 1.5× its 20-day average, so oil-driven sector gaps get caught.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found. G24.DE is Scout24 (German property portal), about 71, with no Oct 9 news. Likely a sector rebound in AI-disrupted internet/software names, or buyback support (up to €350M).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: a mid-cap Xetra/MDAX internet stock that no strategy lists. With no news catalyst, a +3.85% drift or rebound would also fail news-reactive and gap/volume filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a liquid-mid-cap DE/EU screen (e.g. MDAX names with ADV > €20M) to the momentum universe, requiring close-to-close ≥ +3% and volume ≥ 1.5× the 20-day average, so unflagged sector rebounds like this are caught.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed stock-specific news found; likely a sector-wide semiconductor-equipment bounce on the AI-capex theme ahead of ASML's Q3 results (~Oct 14).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BESI is a mid-cap Dutch semiconductor-equipment name on Euronext Amsterdam. A sector-beta move with no company news gives a news-reactive bot no trigger, and a momentum filter likely ignored a +3.8% move on a volatile stock.
top_movers.suggestion: Add BESI.AS, ASM International and other AEX/AMX semi-equipment names to the momentum universe, and add a sector-relative trigger that fires when the ASML/ASMI basket gaps up ≥2% on above-average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed driver found for 2026-10-09. An -11.9% single-day drop in dialysis provider Fresenius Medical Care looks like a guidance cut or pre-announcement, but searches returned nothing dated today.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: FME.DE is a mid/large-cap German healthcare name on Xetra, and no strategy covers it. A sudden unscheduled gap-down also gives a long-only momentum or mean-reversion bot no entry signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add DAX/MDAX healthcare constituents (FME.DE, etc.) to the news-reactive universe, with a watchlist rule that flags any name dropping more than 8% on 2x average volume for manual or reversal-candidate review.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed company-specific driver found. Likely a continuation of the DAX sell-off (high yields and oil) and weakness in Fresenius Medical Care, in which Fresenius holds a stake; the Oct 9 date is unverified.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: Fresenius is a large-cap German healthcare name that no strategy's universe includes. The drop also looks macro or sector-driven with no discrete catalyst, so a news-reactive bot would have had no trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add DAX-40 healthcare large caps (FRE.DE, FME.DE) to the mean-reversion universe, with a sector-wide-selloff flag (e.g. index down ≥1% and name down ≥4%). Shorting is not available, so this only helps on the rebound.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 9 Oct. Searches returned no SDLF.L announcement that day, and I couldn't confirm the issuer or ticker mapping, so this is likely a technical or sector move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. It is probably a small or mid-cap, or a niche or ETF-type London listing, that none of the strategies screen. A -4.95% drift with no news also wouldn't trip a news-reactive or gap trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a daily 'unmapped mover' check that logs any uk-eu ticker moving ≥4% outside all strategy universes, so we can see whether widening the LSE universe (e.g. a min ADV £1m floor) would be worthwhile.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news found. Likely continued selling after VW's mid-Sept 2026 profit warning (2026 margin guided to ≤1%, ~€10bn Porsche-led charges, weak China) and sector weakness.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: VOW3.DE is a large-cap German auto name on Xetra that no strategy includes. It was also a slow-bleed downtrend after a warning three weeks ago, not a fresh gap, so event-driven filters had no trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap DAX/Euro Stoxx 50 names to the mean-reversion/momentum universe, with a 'post-profit-warning downtrend' flag (e.g. 20-day return below -10%). The flag would block long entries and could drive a short or avoid list.
